He dispatched ten leading generals in two forces to capture Song Jiang, and they charged out of the city. The five generals on the southern hills were Wu Zhi, Zhao Yi, Chao Zhong, Yuan Xing, and Su Jing; the northern hill route was likewise assigned five leading generals: Wen Kerang, Cui Yu, Lian Ming, Mao Di, and Tang Fengshi. The northern and southern forces comprised ten leading generals in all, each commanding three thousand horse and foot. Around midnight the gates opened, and the troops at both ends charged out together. As Song Jiang and Dai Zong poured libations and burned paper offerings, they suddenly heard a great roar rise below the bridge. Fan Rui and Ma Lin lay in ambush on the left, and Shi Xiu on the right, each with five thousand men. When they saw fire rise on the road ahead, they too lit their signal fires, split into two forces, and pursued and slaughtered the troops from the northern and southern hills. Seeing that preparations had been made, the southern troops hastily retreated by their former route; Song's troops pursued them on both sides. Wen Kerang led the other four generals hastily back across the river, but behind Baoshu Pagoda Hill they unexpectedly ran into Ruan Xiao'er, Ruan Xiaowu, and Meng Kang, who charged out with five thousand troops and cut off their retreat. Mao Di was captured alive, while Tang Fengshi was stabbed to death in a flurry of spears. On the southern hill, Wu Zhi likewise led the other four generals back in haste as Song's troops pursued them, only to encounter Li Kui, Bao Xu, Xiang Chong, and Li Gun at Dingxiang Bridge, charging out with five hundred infantrymen. The two shield-bearers charged straight into their midst, brandishing their barbarian shields as their flying blades flashed from their sheaths. Yuan Xing was promptly cut down, Bao Xu hacked Su Jing to death, and Li Kui split Zhao Yi with his axe. More than half the troops were driven into the lake and drowned. On hearing this, Song Jiang felt equal parts anxiety and joy, and asked how the generals and troops had fared. Dai Zong replied, “I know all the details of the fighting there, and I also have the official dispatch here. Please do not distress yourself, Commander.” Song Jiang said, “Can it be that I have lost several more of my brothers? Do not conceal anything from me; tell me truthfully what happened.” Dai Zong said, “Ever since Vanguard Commander Lu set out to take Dusong Pass, he found high mountains rising on both sides, with only a single road running between them. The fortress was built on the mountain. Beside it stood a great tree several dozen zhang tall, from which every surrounding place could be seen; below it grew dense, tangled stands of pine. Three rebel generals guarded the pass: their leader was called Wu Sheng, the second was Jiang Yin, and the third Wei Heng. At first they came down from the pass day after day to fight Lin Chong. Lin Chong wounded Jiang Yin with his serpent spear, after which Wu Sheng dared not descend but merely defended the pass from above. Later Li Tianrun arrived with four more generals as reinforcements: Li Dayou, Zhang Jian, Zhang Tao, and Yao Yi. The next day they descended from the pass to fight. Li Tianyou was the first rebel to ride out and engaged Lü Fang. After some fifty or sixty bouts, Lü Fang stabbed Li Tianyou to death with his halberd. The rebels withdrew into the pass and would not come down again. After waiting below the pass for several days, Vanguard Commander Lu, seeing how steep and perilous the ridge was, sent Ou Peng, Deng Fei, Li Zhong, and Zhou Tong up the mountain to scout a route. Unexpectedly, Li Tianrun, intent on avenging his brother, led the rebel troops charging down from the pass and cut down Zhou Tong with his very first stroke. Li Zhong escaped wounded; had help come any later, they would all have been finished. The other three generals were rescued and brought back to camp. The next day, Dong Ping, the ‘General of the Twin Spears,’ impatiently set out for revenge. He reined in below the pass and loudly cursed the rebel generals, but a cannon suddenly fired down from above. The blast injured Dong Ping's left arm. Back at camp he could no longer wield his spears, so his arm was bound in splints. He was determined to go and take revenge the next day, but Vanguard Commander Lu stopped him, and he did not go. After one night he judged his arm recovered. Without informing Vanguard Commander Lu, he conferred privately with Zhang Qing, and the two set out on foot toward the pass. Li Tianrun and Zhang Tao came down from the pass to meet them in battle. Dong Ping sought to capture Li Tianrun and fought on foot with his spear. Li Tianrun met him with a long spear, and they fought for ten bouts. Dong Ping's heart was set only on fighting, but his left hand would not answer when he wielded the spear, so he was forced to retreat. Li Tianrun pursued him down from the pass, whereupon Zhang Qing leveled his spear and thrust at Li Tianrun. Li Tianrun dodged behind a pine tree, and Zhang Qing's spear struck deep into its trunk. When he urgently tried to pull it free, it was stuck fast and would not come loose. Li Darun countered with a spear thrust that struck him squarely in the belly and felled him to the ground. Seeing Zhang Qing felled by the spear, Dong Ping hurried forward with both spears to fight. But Zhang Tao caught him unawares from behind and slashed him across the waist, cutting Dong Ping in two. When Vanguard Commander Lu learned of this, he rushed to the rescue, but the enemy troops had already withdrawn into the pass, and there was no stratagem he could employ below it. He then had the married couple Sun Xin and Madam Gu disguise themselves as refugees. They entered the deep mountains and found a narrow path, then led Li Li, Tang Long, Shi Qian, and Bai Sheng along it past the pass. At midnight they stole up into the fortress and set fires. When the rebel generals saw fire rising within the pass, they knew Song's troops had already penetrated it, so they all abandoned the stronghold and fled.

p.src: Song Jiang and his officers returned to the main camp on Gaoting Mountain and rested. When he took his seat in the command tent and reflected that two more officers, Suo Chao and Deng Fei, had been lost, his heart was deeply troubled. Wu Yong advised him, “With such fierce officers in the city, we must take it by stratagem and must not meet them head-on.” Song Jiang said, “If we keep losing soldiers and officers like this, what plan can capture the city?” Wu Yong replied, “Let the Vanguard first coordinate matters at every gate, and then lead the army to attack the North Barrier Gate. The troops in the city will certainly come out to meet us. We shall pretend to lose and feign flight, luring the rebel forces far from the walls. When a cannon sounds the signal, all the gates will be attacked at once. Once the troops at any one gate enter the city, they are to set fires as a signal. The rebels will surely be unable to aid one another, and we shall win a great victory.” Song Jiang immediately summoned Dai Zong and ordered him to carry the instructions. The next day, he ordered Guan Sheng to lead a large body of troops beneath the North Barrier Gate and challenge the enemy. Drums thundered on the wall. Shi Bao led his army out of the city and crossed weapons with Guan Sheng. Before ten bouts had passed, Guan Sheng hastily retreated. As Shi Bao's troops pursued, Ling Zhen fired the signal cannon. At the sound of the signal cannon, battle cries rose at every gate, and all forces attacked the city together. Now Deputy Vanguard Lu Junyi had led Lin Chong and the others to deploy their troops against Houchao Gate. When they reached the foot of the wall, they saw that the gate stood open and the drawbridge was down. Eager to claim the first merit, Liu Tang charged straight into the city alone, mounted on his horse with blade in hand. Seeing Liu Tang gallop toward them, the defenders atop the wall severed the ropes with an axe, dropping the portcullis. Alas for the valiant Liu Tang—horse and rider alike were crushed to death beneath the gate. The city of Hangzhou had originally been built as the capital of King Qian, who had established a triple gateway: an outer portcullis beyond the barrier, a pair of great iron-plated doors in the middle, and another palisade gate within. The moment Liu Tang charged beneath the gate, the portcullis above had already been released. With ambush troops stationed on both sides as well, how could Liu Tang possibly have survived? Seeing that Liu Tang had been lost, Lin Chong and Huyan Zhuo led their troops back to camp and reported to Lu Junyi. None of the forces could enter through their assigned gates, so they had no choice but to withdraw for the time being and send a messenger racing to inform Vanguard Song's main camp. When Song Jiang heard that Liu Tang too had been lost, crushed beneath the portcullis at Houchao Gate, he wept bitterly and cried, “What a cruel death for this brother of ours! Ever since he swore brotherhood in Yuncheng County and followed Heavenly King Chao to Liangshan Marsh, he endured hardship for so many years and never knew happiness. In scores upon scores of battles, he escaped a hundred deaths to win one life, and never once lost his fighting spirit. Who could have imagined that he would die here today!” Military Strategist Wu Yong said, “This was no sound method. The plan failed and cost us a brother instead. For now, order the forces at every gate to withdraw. We shall devise another course.”

p.src: Song Jiang burned with impatience, longing to avenge the wrong and wipe away the hatred, and sighed without cease. Black Whirlwind, one of his men, said, “Brother, set your mind at ease. Tomorrow Bao Xu, Xiang Chong, Li Gun, and I will capture that scoundrel Shi Bao, whatever it takes!” Song Jiang said, “That man is a formidable champion. How could you possibly get near him?” Li Kui said, “I do not believe it! If I fail to catch him tomorrow, I will not come back to face you, brother.” Song Jiang said, “Just be careful and vigilant. Do not take him lightly.” Black Whirlwind Li Kui returned to his own tent, had great bowls filled with wine and large platters piled with meat, and invited Bao Xu, Xiang Chong, and Li Gun to drink. He said, “The four of us have always fought together as one band. Today I boasted rashly before our vanguard brother that we would capture that scoundrel Shi Bao tomorrow. You three must not lose heart.” Bao Xu said, “Brother has ordered the cavalry forward today, and he will order them forward tomorrow as well. Let us pledge tonight that tomorrow we will advance with one heart and capture that scoundrel Shi Bao. All four of us must show our mettle!” Early the next morning, Li Kui and the other three ate and drank until they were full and tipsy, then took up their weapons and left the camp, asking their vanguard brother to watch them fight. Seeing that all four were half drunk, Song Jiang said, “Brothers, do not make sport of your lives!” Li Kui said, “Brother, do not underestimate us!” Song Jiang said, “I only hope your deeds live up to your words!” Song Jiang mounted his horse and, taking the four cavalry officers Guan Sheng, Ou Peng, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng with him, rode beneath the northern gate, where they beat the drums, waved their banners, and challenged the enemy to battle. Li Kui, seething with impatience, gripped his twin axes and stood before the horses; Bao Xu thrust out his broad-bladed sword and glared with his fearsome eyes, waiting only for the fighting to begin; Xiang Chong and Li Gun each carried a round shield fitted with twenty-four throwing knives, and crouched on either flank with iron spears leveled. Then gongs sounded from the city wall. Shi Bao, mounted on a pale yellow horse and wielding his Wind-Cleaving Saber, led two chief officers out of the city to meet the enemy: Wu Zhi on his right and Lian Ming on his left. The three officers had only just emerged from the city when Li Kui, a man who feared neither Heaven nor Earth, let out a mighty roar, and all four charged straight at Shi Bao’s horse. Shi Bao raised his Wind-Cleaving Saber to meet them, but they were already upon him. With one stroke of his axe, Li Kui hewed through the horse’s leg. Shi Bao leaped down and fled for shelter among the cavalry. Bao Xu had already cut Lian Ming from his horse with a single stroke. The two shield-bearers swiftly sent their throwing knives flying; through the air they flashed like jade fish leaping wildly and silver leaves crossing one another. When Song Jiang led the cavalry in a charge toward the city wall, beams and stones came raining down upon them from above. Fearing disaster, Song Jiang hastily ordered a retreat. But Bao Xu had already rushed through the city gate, and Song Jiang could only cry out in anguish. Shi Bao was lying in ambush inside the gate. Seeing Bao Xu burst in, he sprang from the side and with a single stroke cut him in two. Xiang Chong and Li Gun hurriedly guarded Li Kui as they withdrew. Song Jiang’s forces retreated to their main camp. Having lost Bao Xu as well, Song Jiang grew still more sorrowful, while Li Kui ran back to camp in tears. Wu Yong said, “This was no sound plan either. Though we slew one of their officers, we lost Li Kui’s lieutenant in return.”

p.src: While everyone was sunk in distress, Xie Zhen and Xie Bao arrived at the camp with a report. When Song Jiang asked for the full particulars, Xie Zhen reported, “My younger brother and I scouted more than twenty li beyond the southern gate to a place called Fan Village. There we saw several dozen boats moored in a line along the riverbank. When we went down to question them, we learned that they were grain-transport vessels under Assessor Yuan of Fuyang County. I was about to kill them, but the man himself wept and said, ‘We are all loyal subjects of the Great Song. Fang La has repeatedly burdened us with arbitrary levies, and anyone who refuses has his entire family put to death. Now that the imperial army has come to destroy him, we hoped only to see days of peace again. Who could have imagined that we would instead meet an untimely death?’ His words were so heartfelt that I could not bear to kill him, so I asked, ‘Then why have you come here?’ He replied, ‘Fang Tianding recently issued an order to every county, commanding them to scour the villages and levy fifty thousand shi of polished grain. As the man in charge, I collected five thousand shi and was bringing it ahead of the rest for delivery. But now that we have reached this place, the great armies are besieging the city and fighting, so we dare not proceed and have anchored here.’ Once I had learned all the details, I came especially to report them to our commander.” Wu Yong was delighted. “This opportunity is Heaven-sent. We shall certainly win merit by means of those grain boats. Let the vanguard issue an order at once: you two brothers shall lead the party, taking the artillerist Ling Zhen along with Du Qian, Li Yun, Shi Yong, Zou Yuan, Zou Run, Li Li, Bai Sheng, Mu Chun, and Tang Long. The three married couples—Wang Ying and Hu Sanniang, Sun Xin and Gu Dasao, and Zhang Qing and Sun Erniang—shall disguise themselves as boatmen and boatwomen. None of you is to speak; mingle among the crews at the stern. Once you have slipped into the city in the confusion, fire a rapid volley of cannon as the signal, and I will personally deploy troops here to support you.” Xie Zhen and Xie Bao summoned Assessor Yuan ashore and conveyed Vanguard Song’s orders: “Since you are loyal subjects of the Song, you may follow this plan. When the affair succeeds, you will surely be richly rewarded.”

p.src: And where is Ruan Xiaoqi?" Zhang Heng replied, "I am not Zhang Heng." Song Jiang said, "If you are not Zhang Heng, then who are you?" Zhang Heng said, "I am your younger brother Zhang Shun. Outside Yongjin Gate, I was pierced to death by a hail of spears and arrows. My solitary shade remained wandering upon the waters until the Dragon Lord of the West Lake and Lake Zhenze took pity on me, appointed me Protector of Jinhua, and kept me as a deity in the Dragon Palace beneath the waters. Today, when you broke through the city, my spirit fastened itself to Fang Tianding and followed him out after midnight. I saw my elder brother Zhang Heng in the great river, so I borrowed his body, sped ashore, pursued the villain to the foot of Five Clouds Mountain, slew him, and came straight here to see you." As soon as he had spoken, he suddenly collapsed to the ground. Song Jiang personally helped him up. Zhang Heng opened his eyes and saw Song Jiang and the commanders, with swords and spears thick as a forest and soldiers massed all around. He said, "Can it be that I have met you in the Yellow Springs?" Weeping, Song Jiang said, "Just now your brother Zhang Shun possessed your body and killed that villain Fang Tianding. You have not died. We are all living men, so collect yourself." Zhang Heng said, "If that is so, then my brother is already dead!" Song Jiang said, "Zhang Shun meant to pass beneath the waters of the West Lake, force his way through a water gate, enter the city, and set it afire. But outside Yongjin Gate, as he tried to scale the wall, he was discovered and pierced to death by a hail of spears and arrows." Hearing this, Zhang Heng cried aloud, "Brother!" Then he suddenly fell senseless. When the others looked at Zhang Heng, his limbs would not move and his eyes were dim; his seven earthly spirits drifted away, and his three celestial souls vanished into the distance. Truly: If he has not gone at the summons of the General of the Five Paths, then surely the two demons of Impermanence are urging him away. What ultimately became of Zhang Heng's life after he fainted will be revealed in the next chapter.
